plans.note: Only the preamble is exposed in the outline; a Master Services Agreement of this type will carry a limitation-of-liability article. Search the body for 'Limitation of Liability', 'consequential', 'aggregate liability' and check cap size, mutuality and carve-outs (IP indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence/willful misconduct).

Locate the indemnification article in the unexposed body; confirm Kubient indemnifies AP for third-party IP infringement and its own negligence/misconduct, and that any AP-side indemnity is narrow and reciprocal. Cross-check against the liability cap for a carve-out.

Presence check: scan the body for any covenant restricting AP from operating competing businesses or engaging other ad-tech/inventory platforms. Frequently absent in vendor MSAs, but the truncated outline does not permit a finding of absence.

Presence check for exclusive-supply or 'sole provider' language, including any exclusivity embedded in the services/scope or fee sections. Ad-tech MSAs sometimes place exclusivity in an order form or exhibit — check any schedules referenced from the body.

Direction check: look in the pricing/fees provisions for 'most favoured', 'best terms' or 'no less favourable' language. Only flag if the obligation runs from AP to Kubient; MFN in AP's favour is welcome and should not be redlined.

Presence check for a non-solicitation covenant, often sited near confidentiality or general provisions. Assess duration, whether it binds AP (mutuality) and whether general advertising/unsolicited applications are carved out.

Examine the term-and-termination article referenced by the defined term 'Initial Term'; confirm AP has termination for convenience on reasonable notice without penalty and that Kubient cannot terminate for convenience mid-term.

Same term article as T4C ('Initial Term' is defined): check for automatic renewal, the non-renewal notice window and any renewal price uplift. A missing uplift cap is a rationale note, not a deviation.

Look in the general/miscellaneous provisions for governing law and venue. Kubient is New York-based, so New York law with New York courts is likely and acceptable; flag only foreign law or mandatory offshore arbitration.

Check the miscellaneous provisions for the assignment clause; confirm AP may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger or asset sale, and that Kubient has no termination or consent right triggered by AP's change of control.

Direction check in the intellectual property / data provisions: AP must own its content, inventory data and any paid-for deliverables; flag any assignment or broad licence of AP data or IP to Kubient beyond what is needed to deliver the services.

Review the platform/licence grant in the services article: confirm scope extends to AP affiliates and contractors acting on AP's behalf and that the grant is not revocable at Kubient's discretion during the term.

Search the fees/compliance provisions for any Kubient right to audit AP usage or records; test frequency, advance notice, business-hours limits, confidentiality and who bears cost. Distinguish from AP's own reporting/verification rights, which we do not flag.

Direction check: look for liquidated damages, early-termination fees or penalty language payable by AP in the fees or termination provisions. Service credits running to AP are beneficial and should not be flagged.
Check the representations and warranties article for a performance/services warranty, its duration and remedy (re-performance, then refund), and note any broad 'AS IS' disclaimer that would gut it.

Insurance is often omitted from short ad-tech MSAs and may sit in an exhibit; search the body for 'insurance', 'certificate of insurance', 'cyber' before concluding it is missing. Kubient handles AP data, so coverage including cyber/tech E&O is expected.
Presence check in the fees/order form provisions for minimum spend, minimum volume or take-or-pay commitments binding AP, and whether an exit or shortfall remedy exists.

Check the effects-of-termination provisions for return/deletion of AP data in a usable format and any transition or wind-down assistance obligation; if only deletion is addressed, note the gap on data return and migration support.
